page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-8 is an arm64-based virtual machine belonging to the t2a server family. It is equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Ampere ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 3.0 GHz. The hardware configuration features 8 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, 32.0 GB of system memory providing 4.0 GB per core, and cache sizes of 64 KB L1d, 1.0 MB L2, and 32 MB L3. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across several multi-threaded and memory-bound workloads. The instance achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 14472.4 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6000.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 563.91 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 87.42 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1073.0 and a weak Passmark CPU score of 6205.54. Cryptographic and text processing capabilities are also limited, with a weak Passmark CPU encryption test result of 1300.22 and a poor LLM text generation speed of 32.29 tokens/sec for small models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the t2a-standard-8 offers a balanced resource density of 4 GB of RAM per dedicated ARM core, making it a viable option for scale-out workloads that benefit from physical core isolation without hyperthreading. It is suited for static web serving, where it achieved a throughput of 10.09 GB/sec, Redis deployments with 10.91 million SET operations per second, and multi-threaded software compilation. It is less suitable for single-threaded tasks, heavy cryptographic operations, or large language model inference.
